bull_bear.body:
- Industry leading market share in the Extra High Voltage (EHV) Power Cable business in India, including turnkey end-to-end solutions, built on longstanding experience and strong credentials
- India's first of its kind VCV (Vertical Continuous Vulcanization) EHV cable manufacturing technology, also equipped to manufacture EHV HVDC cables
- Established supplier of power cables up to the 400 kV voltage grade - one of the broadest EHV portfolios in the domestic market
- Flagship 'UNISTAR' brand with strong brand equity, carried alongside the M.P. Birla Group logo, acknowledged as a pioneer and benchmark in the Indian cable industry
- High customer entry barriers in EHV: extensive customisation, quality assurance, uninterrupted supply and pre-qualification approvals favour established players with a proven track record
- Diversified customer base spanning power utilities (State and Central), oil & petrochemicals, mining, steel, cement, shipbuilding, railways, defence and renewables, plus overseas customers
- Diversified supply chain mechanism adopted over the years has kept availability of metals and polymers relatively stable despite a volatile raw-material landscape
- Established export footprint across the Middle East, Europe, Latin America and certain neighbouring countries, supported by advanced manufacturing, product quality and reliable deliveries
- In-house R&D and testing infrastructure (DSIR-recognised R&D lab; NABL-accredited EHV cable laboratories at Satna and Goa)
- Strategic technological collaborations with global industry leaders, including a Manufacturing Agreement with TS Conductor Corp, USA for HTLS conductors
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw Material Price Risk - copper, aluminium, lead and polymer volatility against largely firm-price cable contracts — The prices of international commodities such as copper, aluminium, lead and polymers, the key raw material components, are subject to considerable price volatility, while market prices of cables are generally on a firm price basis. Strict implementation of Quality Control Order(s) by the Government without adequate and competitive local production facilities matching global quality standards for key inputs adds further price-volatility risk and unjustified price increases, and 'green inflation' risk remains high because aluminium and copper have higher-application use cases in energy transition products.
- Working Capital Risk - dependence on infrastructure/industrial capex, budgetary allocations and institutional funding — The Company caters to infrastructural and industrial segments that largely depend on economic buoyancy, budgetary allocation and funding from banks and institutions. An economic setback or curtailment in fund allocation could lead to fund scarcity and delayed realisation of receivables, directly affecting working capital requirements. Mitigated by prioritising customers with sound financial standing, constant follow-up on receivables and lean, symmetric inventories.
- Competition Risk and technology obsolescence - distinct competitive dynamics by voltage grade — In EHV, competition comes from both Indian and overseas manufacturers, with entry barriers requiring performance-record credentials from users on supply and installation to qualify as an eligible bidder plus repeat testing and revalidation of type/design test reports; the Company must keep pace with multinational development and innovation to avoid obsolescence. In HV & MV, new entrants pose price-competitiveness risk. The LV segment is intensely competitive with a proliferation of regional producers of low-quality, low-margin products that has been pernicious to the health of the organised sector.
- Market Demand Risk - historically cyclical power cable demand and direct exposure to Government policy — Demand for power cables has historically been cyclical, and the Company is dependent on the infrastructure sector, industries and OEMs, with Government policies having a direct bearing on demand from various market segments. Partially offset by a broad-based clientele, wide product range and a flexible manufacturing set-up that allows product-mix changes to suit the order and demand pattern.
- Project execution and Liquidated Damage Risk on turnkey contracts — The Company executes several turnkey projects requiring statutory right-of-way permissions from authorities that are outside the control of both the Company and the user, which may defer projects and cause blockage of receivables and cost over-runs. Separately, intense competition forces acceptance of short delivery contracts, and failure to meet the delivery period exposes the Company to imposition of liquidated damages.
- Customer Risk - customer priority shifts, increasing customer power and over-reliance on major customers — The Company is prone to the risk of customers' priority shift, increasing customer power and over-reliance on major customers. Mitigated by staying in constant touch with clientele, providing technical guidance and crisis support to remain 'virtually indispensable', and building a preferred-supplier reputation that creates a quality trust barrier against competition and new entrants.
- External trade barriers, geopolitical fragmentation and rising ESG compliance cost — Global power cables and capacitors trade is increasingly exposed to trade policies and tariffs aimed at protecting local manufacturing, alongside growing protectionism, supply chain disruption, recalibration of international alliances and economic nationalism. Escalating raw material and logistics costs, supply chain bottlenecks from geo-political developments, regional conflicts and social unrest may impact operations. Implementing sustainable manufacturing practices under stringent environment and safety regulations is costly and complex, with limited availability of sustainable materials and standardisation challenges.
- Occupational Health & Safety and environmental footprint of operations (BRSR material issues) — BRSR identifies Occupational Health & Safety as a risk given injury and fatality rates higher than in many other industries, with temporary workers more vulnerable due to limited training and experience; inadequate management can lead to serious human harm, legal consequences and significant financial burdens (accidents increase insurance, litigation and downtime costs). Environmental footprint of operations is also flagged as a risk - biodiversity impact, air emissions, water discharge, natural resource depletion and waste generation - with non-compliance penalties as the stated financial implication.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company is predominantly engaged in the manufacture and/or sale of a wide range of Power Cables from 1.1 kV to 400 kV, Wires and Conductors, Accessories for Cables and Conductors, products for quality power solutions viz. Capacitors and Capacitor Banks, Harmonic Filters, etc. and Turnkey Projects relating thereto. It is also a manufacturer of Power and Control Cables, Optical Fibre Cables and Capacitors, and is actively engaged in executing turnkey projects in the Transmission and Distribution (T&D) segment of the power sector. Its EHV cable facility uses India's first of its kind VCV (Vertical Continuous Vulcanization) technology and is also equipped to manufacture EHV HVDC cables, serving power utilities (State and Central) and private-sector customers in India and 32 overseas countries.

business.body:
- **Power Cables:** Power Cables from 1.1 kV to 400 kV, EHV / HVAC XLPE power cables up to 400 kV, Medium Voltage (MV) cables, Low Voltage (LV) cables, Power and Control Cables, UNISTAR (flagship brand)
- **Wires & Conductors:** Wires and Conductors, Flexible wire and Multicore Flexible Cables, HTLS (High Temperature Low Sag) Conductors with TS Aluminium Encapsulated Composite Core

- **Optical Fibre:** Optical Fibre Cables
- **Quality Power Solutions:** Capacitors and Capacitor Banks, Harmonic Filters, MV automatic power factor control panels
- **Turnkey Projects:** Turnkey projects in the Transmission and Distribution (T&D) segment of the power sector

outlook.body:
- Implement a well-planned strategy of gradual, phased increase in production capacity across all voltage grades of cables and capacitors to cater to increased demand, while controlling costs and meeting sustainability expectations, in order to expand its footprint further in domestic and overseas marketplaces.
- Complete the MV and EHV cables capacity augmentation at Satna (M.P.) and Verna (Goa) begun in FY 2024-25, debottlenecking capacity in phased manner by August/September 2026 to sustain growth momentum and maintain overall market share.
- Undertake technological upgradation and modernisation of the EHV cable facility at Satna with an outlay of Rs 7300 Lakhs, investing in precision manufacturing and flexibility to meet international quality, safety and environmental standards and become more competitive and export oriented.
- Build in-house EHV HVDC cable capability - developing additional capabilities and exploring a technical tie-up - to substitute imports ahead of multiple government HVDC projects and to address surging international HVDC demand.
- Enter the HTLS conductor business under a Manufacturing Agreement with TS Conductor Corp, USA, sourcing the TS Aluminium Encapsulated Composite Core, to drive volume growth in the Conductors business with an expanded portfolio.
- Increase the export orientation of the business, leveraging advanced manufacturing, superior product quality, reliable deliveries and a diverse portfolio across the Middle East, Europe, Latin America and neighbouring countries, on the back of completed prestigious EHV export orders up to 400 kV.
- Preserve manufacturing flexibility - the setup allows seamless transitions between EHV and MV cable production, and the ongoing expansion further enhances the ability to dynamically switch between HV/EHV and MV XLPE insulated power cables to manage fluctuating and asymmetric demand.
- Optimise resources on high-end, high-margin products rather than high-volume low-margin products, so that top-line growth is compensated with a better bottom-line and better returns on capital employed (stated 'good growth plan' over 'growth-trap').
- Develop specialised cable products with enhanced fire safety features and environmentally responsible specifications aligned with market and regulatory expectations, and maintain the established multi-region dealer network to scale the LV cable business.
- Pursue strategic cost management without compromising on margins, with fiscal prudence, cutting discretionary spending and accelerating efficiency to navigate geo-political volatility and ensure operational resilience.
- Continue focus on improved capacity utilisation, reduction of scrap, optimal use of input raw materials and supply-chain strengthening for timely availability of critical raw materials, supporting inventory control and operational efficiency.
- The Company has no subsidiaries (Form AOC-1 Part A: 'Subsidiaries - Not Applicable'), holding only an associate (Vindhya Telelinks Limited) and a joint venture (Birla Furukawa Fibre Optics Private Limited). On the balance sheet, the Notice of the Eighty-First AGM proposes a Special Resolution under Sections 180(1)(c) and 180(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 - in supersession of the resolution passed at the 79th AGM held on 2nd August, 2024 - authorising the Board to borrow, in any manner and in any form (rupee or foreign currency loans/credit facilities, debentures, bonds, inter-corporate deposits, other borrowings and non-fund based facilities), sums that may exceed the aggregate of paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium, subject to a total outstanding cap of Rs 4500 Crores. The AGM's ordinary business also includes declaration of dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended 31st March, 2026. On governance philosophy, the Company states that good corporate governance is a tool for achieving all-round business excellence reflected in enhanced shareholder value, without compromising the need and interest of other stakeholders. Independent Directors' remuneration by way of profit-related commission is capped within an overall maximum limit of 1% per annum of Net Profits computed under Section 198 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Occupational Health & Safety managed through comprehensive safety procedures, risk assessments, assured adherence to occupational health and safety laws, frequent training courses, cultivation of a robust safety culture and continuous observation and enhancement of safety procedures.
- Environmental footprint mitigated through robust environmental management systems, regular assessments, and sustainable practices covering responsible resource consumption, waste reduction initiatives and stakeholder engagement.
- Energy Management treated as a strategic ESG opportunity - improving energy efficiency, broadening the energy mix and incorporating renewable and alternative energy, with a commissioned rooftop solar power plant cited as evidence of the clean-energy commitment and a lever to lower operational costs and reduce exposure to energy price volatility.
- Water Management identified as both risk and opportunity for manufacturing and EPC operations: implement water-efficient technologies, rainwater harvesting, wastewater treatment and reuse systems, and conduct water audits to identify savings.
- Waste Management pursued as an opportunity through minimising waste generation at source, promoting reuse of materials within operations, safe and compliant disposal through certified vendors, proper waste segregation and circular resource use.
- Product Responsibility: invest in R&D for greener materials, meet RoHS / REACH / IEC / TUV standards, ensure product testing and third-party certifications, and promote reclaim or recycling programmes where applicable.
- Sustainable Materials Sourcing to reduce direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions by partnering with suppliers demonstrating lower carbon footprints, encouraging sustainable sourcing practices, and embedding responsible supply chain management into core strategy - also supporting eligibility for green contracts.
- Employee Growth, Training and Learning & Development treated as a material opportunity, with continuous employee upskilling required to keep pace with evolving regulatory standards, new technologies and client expectations in cables and capacitors manufacturing.
- Community Development and Relations: CSR projects carried out directly or through the implementing agency Madhav Prasad Priyamvada Birla Apex Charitable Trust, with the HR department maintaining industrial relations with communities, aimed at securing a social licence to operate.
- Formal governance architecture of ESG-relevant policies: Anti-Corruption or Anti-Bribery Policy, Code of Conduct for Board of Directors and Senior Management, Sourcing with Human Dignity Policy, Non-Discrimination, Diversity and Equal Opportunity Policy, Stakeholder Management Policy, Modern Slavery Policy / Human Dignity Policy, Sustainability Policy, Policy on Responsible Advocacy, Corporate Social Responsibility Policy, and Information Security Management System Policy.
- Stakeholder grievance architecture with defined channels per group - Whistle-Blower Policy for employees and workers, dedicated customer care for product complaints, Supplier Code of Conduct for value chain partners, and Registrar & Share Transfer Agent MUFG Intime India Private Limited plus the Company Secretary for investors - under a Stakeholder Management Policy; in FY 2025-26 complaints filed were 4 (Communities), 4 (Shareholders) and 3 (Customers), with none pending resolution at the close of the year.
- Workforce diversity remains low: women are 1 of 7 Board of Directors (14.29%) and 0 of 3 Key Management Personnel (0.00%); permanent-employee turnover was 8.51% and permanent-worker turnover 12.52% in FY 2025-26.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Universal Cables' entire growth plan is based on organic expansion, and the Company states it sees enough growth opportunities within its existing facilities to implement expansion plans for scaling up manufacturing capacity of LV, MV, HV & EHV Power Cables, flexible wire and multicore Flexible Cables, Capacitors, etc. During FY 2025-26 two projects were completed: the capacity expansion of the flexible wire and Multicore Flexible Cables facility at Verna (Goa), operational at the end of October 2025, and a new Low Voltage power cable facility at Satna (M.P.), operational at the end of March 2026. The larger MV and EHV cables capacity augmentation project was partially commissioned for commercial operations during the third quarter of the year under review and is likely to be fully operational in phased manner by end of August/September 2026; the Company has flagged minor delays in fully operationalising it due to civil construction related delays and other external factors, and says the enhanced capacity will significantly strengthen its MV and EHV manufacturing capabilities. Alongside this, the Company has planned technological upgradation and modernisation of its EHV cable facility at Satna with an outlay of Rs 7300 Lakhs, investing in precision manufacturing and flexibility to meet use-case-specific quality standards and international quality, safety and environmental standards, with the aim of becoming more competitive and export oriented. Beyond cables, the Company is investing in setting up infrastructure for manufacturing and sale of HTLS (High Temperature Low Sag) Conductors with TS Aluminium Encapsulated Composite Core, and plans in-house production of HVDC cables, which are currently imported, ahead of multiple government HVDC projects. Capital expenditure during the year was directed primarily towards production capacity augmentation initiatives aimed at supporting future growth. On the sustainability side, the Company operates rooftop solar plants of 2 MW at Satna and 0.5 MW at Goa plus electricity from a 4 MW wind-solar hybrid project commissioned in July 2024 under a long-term Power Purchase Agreement, and is installing two new sewage treatment plants of 32 KLD and 16 KLD capacity expected to be commissioned in FY 2026-27 on top of existing STP capacity of 200 + 70 KLD.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government schemes - RDSS, Green Energy Corridor, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, National Smart Grid Mission and FAME II - are collectively driving additions to line length, sub-station capacity, smart metering and EV charging infrastructure, shaping a broad and durable demand base.
- Discoms and city utilities are shifting from overhead lines to underground cabling, with metro rail networks, smart city clusters, commercial districts and dense residential zones mandating 11kV and 33kV underground systems, ring main units and compact substations - accelerating uptake of medium-voltage and high-performance cables.
- India's wires and cables industry constitutes about 40% of the electrical industry and is expected to grow 2x GDP growth during FY 2025-2030, driven by capacity expansion, the T&D and real-estate capex cycle and emerging segments such as data centres, EV and mobility, railways and metro expansion.
- Per the Crisil Intelligence Report of February 2026, domestic power cable consumption may grow about 22% in FY 2025-26 after about 45% growth in FY 2024-25, and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 9-11% between FY 2026-27 and FY 2028-29.
- Management expects revenue growth higher than the industry, driven by increased focus on exports, successful completion of prestigious export orders for EHV cables up to 400 kV, and orders in hand as well as in the pipeline.
- EHV Power Cables: VCV lines dedicated to EHV production are fully aligned to meet the anticipated surge in EHV demand, giving a competitive edge through superior product quality and faster delivery timelines; the EHV business is expected to be a key driver of expansion in both domestic and international markets.
- HV & MV Power Cables: demand expected to rise steadily as Government emphasises upgrading power distribution infrastructure and reducing Aggregate Technical & Commercial (AT&C) losses; FY26 growth of around 9% came from optimum capacity utilisation and partial commencement of the MV capacity augmentation project.
- LV Cables & Conductors: FY26 growth of around 16% on most optimum capacity utilisation; ongoing growth in real estate, metro railway projects and smart city developments is expected to further drive LV demand, with volume growth also envisaged in Conductors from the expanded HTLS portfolio.
- Rubber Specialty Cables: revenue up approximately 30% in FY26 with a strong niche position aided by Pressurised Liquid Salt Bath Curing (PLCV) technology - the only one of its kind in India - and in-house compounding; however the conventional rubber cable market is contracting due to substitution by Electron Beam Irradiated Cross-Linked Cables.
- Light Duty Wires & Cables (Goa): aggregate revenue grew around 23% in FY26 driven by production capacity augmentation that became fully operational in Q3, though demand for PVC winding wires and flat cables has plateaued, with the Company positioned as a dedicated supplier to major OEMs.
- Quality Power Solutions: turnover surpassed Rs 179.17 crores for the first time with around 78% growth; demand outlook remains positive on public and private utility and renewable developer initiatives, rising reactive-power-compensation needs, bulk capacitors for solar and wind grid nodes, and harmonic filter banks needed to meet IEEE 519 THD/TDD limits mandated by the Central Electricity Authority.
- The Indian power quality products market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 9% from 2023-2028, from USD 798 Million in 2023 to USD 1.22 Billion in 2028, with capacitor banks contributing around 28.70% of market share in 2028.
- Headwind: highly volatile raw material landscape - copper, aluminium and polymer price swings with expectations of further increases in FY 2026-27 - compounded by rupee volatility against the US dollar and euro, partially mitigated by advocating Price Variation (PV) clauses in customer contracts.
- The Company's leadership position as the foremost producer of EHV cables up to 400 kV with a state-of-the-art VCV process positions it to capture the imminent infrastructure upgrade as electricity consumption grows in India.
- Revenue from Operations of the EHV Power Cable business increased by approximately 33% as a result of a strong order book and gradual increase in production capacity.
- During the year under review, the Company secured certain substantial value contracts, which further strengthened the Company's goodwill and leadership in EHV Cables and related turnkey businesses in domestic and overseas marketplaces.
- The year under review marked a defining milestone in the Company's growth journey with highest ever turnover and profitability, robust orders inflow and strong execution.
- Increased focus on exports with successful completion of prestigious export orders for EHV cables up to 400 kV voltage grade, and orders in hand as well as in the pipeline, are expected to drive revenue growth higher than the industry.

risks.note: The prices of international commodities such as copper, aluminium, lead and polymers, the key raw material components, are subject to considerable price volatility, while market prices of cables are generally on a firm price basis. Strict implementation of Quality Control Order(s) by the Government without adequate and competitive local production facilities matching global quality standards for key inputs adds further price-volatility risk and unjustified price increases, and 'green inflation' risk remains high because aluminium and copper have higher-application use cases in energy transition products.
risks.risk: Raw Material Price Risk - copper, aluminium, lead and polymer volatility against largely firm-price cable contracts

risks.note: The Company caters to infrastructural and industrial segments that largely depend on economic buoyancy, budgetary allocation and funding from banks and institutions. An economic setback or curtailment in fund allocation could lead to fund scarcity and delayed realisation of receivables, directly affecting working capital requirements. Mitigated by prioritising customers with sound financial standing, constant follow-up on receivables and lean, symmetric inventories.
risks.risk: Working Capital Risk - dependence on infrastructure/industrial capex, budgetary allocations and institutional funding

risks.note: In EHV, competition comes from both Indian and overseas manufacturers, with entry barriers requiring performance-record credentials from users on supply and installation to qualify as an eligible bidder plus repeat testing and revalidation of type/design test reports; the Company must keep pace with multinational development and innovation to avoid obsolescence. In HV & MV, new entrants pose price-competitiveness risk. The LV segment is intensely competitive with a proliferation of regional producers of low-quality, low-margin products that has been pernicious to the health of the organised sector.
risks.risk: Competition Risk and technology obsolescence - distinct competitive dynamics by voltage grade

risks.note: Demand for power cables has historically been cyclical, and the Company is dependent on the infrastructure sector, industries and OEMs, with Government policies having a direct bearing on demand from various market segments. Partially offset by a broad-based clientele, wide product range and a flexible manufacturing set-up that allows product-mix changes to suit the order and demand pattern.
risks.risk: Market Demand Risk - historically cyclical power cable demand and direct exposure to Government policy

risks.note: The Company executes several turnkey projects requiring statutory right-of-way permissions from authorities that are outside the control of both the Company and the user, which may defer projects and cause blockage of receivables and cost over-runs. Separately, intense competition forces acceptance of short delivery contracts, and failure to meet the delivery period exposes the Company to imposition of liquidated damages.
risks.risk: Project execution and Liquidated Damage Risk on turnkey contracts

risks.note: The Company is prone to the risk of customers' priority shift, increasing customer power and over-reliance on major customers. Mitigated by staying in constant touch with clientele, providing technical guidance and crisis support to remain 'virtually indispensable', and building a preferred-supplier reputation that creates a quality trust barrier against competition and new entrants.
risks.risk: Customer Risk - customer priority shifts, increasing customer power and over-reliance on major customers

risks.note: Global power cables and capacitors trade is increasingly exposed to trade policies and tariffs aimed at protecting local manufacturing, alongside growing protectionism, supply chain disruption, recalibration of international alliances and economic nationalism. Escalating raw material and logistics costs, supply chain bottlenecks from geo-political developments, regional conflicts and social unrest may impact operations. Implementing sustainable manufacturing practices under stringent environment and safety regulations is costly and complex, with limited availability of sustainable materials and standardisation challenges.
risks.risk: External trade barriers, geopolitical fragmentation and rising ESG compliance cost

risks.note: BRSR identifies Occupational Health & Safety as a risk given injury and fatality rates higher than in many other industries, with temporary workers more vulnerable due to limited training and experience; inadequate management can lead to serious human harm, legal consequences and significant financial burdens (accidents increase insurance, litigation and downtime costs). Environmental footprint of operations is also flagged as a risk - biodiversity impact, air emissions, water discharge, natural resource depletion and waste generation - with non-compliance penalties as the stated financial implication.
risks.risk: Occupational Health & Safety and environmental footprint of operations (BRSR material issues)
